subject: Access provisioning: role roster, delegation model, and SSO/SCIM clarifications
messages:
From: Alex Murphy <alex.murphy@graftonbank.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: security@graftonbank.com
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFI: clarification on SSO, SCIM and admin delegation model

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the RFI packet you sent last week. Our security and identity teams reviewed it and we have a few clarifying questions before we move this to procurement:

1) SSO: We see SAML 2.0 listed, can you confirm support for OIDC/OAuth2 dynamic client registration and whether Redwood supports SP-initiated OIDC flows for both web and mobile clients?

2) SCIM: Does your SCIM implementation support bulk provisioning and attribute-level mapping (custom attributes)? What is the sync cadence and how do you handle transient failures (retry policy, dead-letter)?

3) RBAC/admin controls: We need an example role roster and recommended delegation model for a bank with ~1,200 end-users and 25 admins. Specifically how do you handle: delegated admin scoping per-tenant, session timeouts for admin sessions, and audit trails for privileged changes?

4) Evidence: Please provide a sample SCIM schema, a role matrix, and a short snippet of sync logs (redacted). Also helpful would be a diagram of the SSO negotiation flow including fallback policies.

Target timeline: procurement would like answers by end of week (10/09). Is that feasible?

Regards,
Alex Murphy
Senior IAM Architect
Grafton Bank
alex.murphy@graftonbank.com

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Murphy <alex.murphy@graftonbank.com>
Cc: security@graftonbank.com, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: clarification on SSO, SCIM and admin delegation model

Alex —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front and then I've attached the requested artifacts. Will hit your deadline (10/09) with any follow-ups.

1) SSO: Redwood supports both SAML 2.0 and OIDC (including SP-initiated OIDC auth code flow). We also support dynamic client registration for OIDC (RFC 7591) and token revocation endpoints per RFC 7009. Mobile SDKs can use PKCE for public clients.

2) SCIM: We support SCIM 2.0 with bulk operations (per RFC 7644) and attribute-level mapping via a configurable attribute map in the Console. Sync cadence is configurable (near-real-time via event-driven webhooks or scheduled delta-syncs every 5 minutes). Failure handling: automatic retries with exponential backoff (up to 5 attempts), and failed items are written to a dead-letter queue that can be exported.

3) RBAC/admin controls: Attached is an admin role matrix and a recommended delegation model that separates tenant admins from privileged infra admins. Session idle-timeout and max session length are configurable per role (defaults: 15m idle, 8h max). All admin actions are logged with immutable event IDs, and we provide daily audit exports and real-time streaming of admin events to customer SIEM via webhook or syslog.

4) Evidence: Attached: redwood_scim_schema_v1.json, redwood_admin_role_matrix.xlsx, scim_sync_logs_sample.txt, and a short SSO flow diagram (redwood_sso_flow_diagram.pdf).

If you want, Ben (cc'd) can run a short joint call with identity ops to walk through mapping details.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

+1 (415) 555-0142

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 09:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: clarification on SSO, SCIM and admin delegation model

Alex/Kim —

Quick notes from engineering/solutions:
- For large banks we recommend using event-driven SCIM (webhooks) for near-real-time provisioning and a scheduled full-sync overnight for reconciliation.
- For custom attributes, we can persist up to 200 custom attributes per user; we advise namespacing (grafton_ext:employee_id) to avoid collisions.
- Regarding RBAC: the attached role matrix includes a "delegated tenant admin" role that scopes to tenant_id and excludes privileged config changes (those are only infra-admin). We also support time-bound elevation (just-in-time admin) via the Console with optional MFA for elevation.

One action: we need to confirm whether Grafton wants audit exports pushed into your SIEM (we can set up a trial pipeline). If yes, what syslog/ingestion endpoint should we use?

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Ben/Kim — thanks, useful. A couple follow-ups before we sign off:

• Can you confirm retention windows for admin audit logs (how long are events retained in your platform by default and can we request extended retention)?
• For JIT elevation, does Redwood emit an approval event we can correlate in our access reviews?

We'd like sample exports sent to our SIEM demo endpoint: demo-siem.grafton.int:514 (syslog over TLS). Also please include the JSON schema you use for admin events so our SIEM mapping team can ingest correctly.

One last ask: Procurement wants the final artifact bundle on 10/09 COB and a short 30-min tech call the week of 10/12 to walk the team through role-mapping and SCIM attribute mapping.

Alex

Alex —

Confirming next steps and deliverables:
- We'll deliver the full artifact bundle (role matrix, SCIM schema, sample admin event schema, redacted sync logs, SSO flow diagram, and SOC 2 excerpt) by 2026-10-09 COB.
- Retention: admin audit events are retained 90 days by default in the Console; we can provision extended retention (up to 3 years) as an add-on and we will include an export package for 365/730/1095-day windows as requested.
- JIT elevation: Redwood emits a correlated approval event with a unique request_id that is included in the admin event export; you can use that to reconcile access reviews. Sample event schema attached (admin_event_schema.json).
- We'll push a one-way stream to demo-siem.grafton.int:514 over syslog/TLS for the trial; Sean will coordinate the connection details and certificate exchange.

Proposed tech call: Tue 2026-10-13 10:00 AM ET (30 min). Please confirm.
